question: Does the solution require that components be installed on the client asset?
text: Does the solution require that components be installed on the client asset? This may limit business processes where nonenterprise-owned assets are used or desired, such as BYOD or cross-agency collaborations.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

question: Does the solution work where the business process resources exist entirely on enterprise premises?
text: Does the solution work where the business process resources exist entirely on enterprise premises? Some solutions assume that requested resources will reside in the cloud (so-called north-south traffic) and not within an enterprise perimeter (east-west traffic). The location of candidate business process resources will influence candidate solutions as well as the ZTA for the process.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

question: Does the solution provide a means to log interactions for analysis?
text: Does the solution provide a means to log interactions for analysis? A key component of ZT is the collection and use of data related to the process flow that feeds back into the PE when making access decisions.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

question: Does the solution provide broad support for different applications, services, and protocols?
text: Does the solution provide broad support for different applications, services, and protocols? Some solutions may support a broad range of protocols (web, secure shell [SSH], etc.) and transports (IPv4 and IPv6), while others may only work with a narrow focus such as web or email.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

question: Does the solution require changes to subject behavior?
text: Does the solution require changes to subject behavior? Some solutions may require additional steps to perform a given workflow. This may change how enterprise subjects perform the workflow.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf
